passage:
Mateo: Kowalski is the best keeper in the league, end of discussion. Three clean sheets in his last five games!
Ines: He's let in 41 goals this season, more than any other starting keeper.
Mateo: Those last five games show who he really is. The rest is noise.
cue: Those last five games show who he really is. The rest is noise.
explanation: Mateo builds his case on the five games that flatter Kowalski and dismisses the rest of the season. The full record, not the best stretch, is what shows how good a keeper is.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: Mateo isn't stuck with too little information; the whole season is available and he chooses only the stretch that suits him.

title: 31% returns. Imagine what your savings could do.
passage: Last year the Harborline Growth Fund returned 31%, beating the market by a mile. Our advisors are available seven days a week, and getting started takes five minutes, with a minimum of just $500. *Annual returns 2021-2024: -8%, 2%, -4%, 5%. Past performance does not guarantee future results.
cue: Last year the Harborline Growth Fund returned 31%, beating the market by a mile
explanation: Harborline headlines its one standout year and tucks the losing and weak years into the small print. Judged over five years, the fund looks far less impressive.

whyNot.fal_texas_sharpshooter: Harborline isn't inventing a pattern after the fact; it simply spotlights its best year and buries the rest.

title: Great news from our spring results!
passage: Dear families, our spring reading results are in! Grade 3 scores rose 9 points, the biggest jump in the district. That tells us the new literacy approach we introduced in grades 3 to 5 this year is working, and we'll expand it next fall. Thank you, teachers! (Grade 4 and 5 numbers are in the full report on the portal; new tests always take a year to settle.)
cue: That tells us the new literacy approach we introduced in grades 3 to 5 this year is working
explanation: The new approach runs in three grades, but Mr. Lindahl cites only the one that improved and tucks the other two into a portal report with an excuse. The results he sidelines are exactly the ones that could undercut his claim.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: He isn't short of data: he has results for all three grades and showcases only the one that looks good.

title: Sparrowdale says its calendar redesign is a hit with users
passage: Sparrowdale Software says its redesigned calendar app is winning people over, pointing to more than 2,000 five-star reviews posted since the update launched. The new layout does load faster, according to independent tests. The company's statement did not mention the app's overall rating, which has fallen from 4.6 to 3.1 stars since the update.
cue: pointing to more than 2,000 five-star reviews posted since the update launched
explanation: Sparrowdale highlights the glowing reviews and skips the overall rating, which has dropped sharply. A few thousand fans can coexist with many more unhappy users.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: 2,000 reviews isn't a tiny sample; the issue is that Sparrowdale counts only the favorable ones.

source: Text thread · Lena (agent) and the Okonkwos
passage:
Lena: Seven similar homes sold on Alder Street this year. The three nicest went for $610k to $640k.
Chidi: So where should we list?
Lena: Those three are what buyers will compare yours to, so $650k is realistic. No need to get hung up on the others.
cue: Those three are what buyers will compare yours to, so $650k is realistic
explanation: Lena has seven comparable sales but prices the house off only the three highest. Buyers and appraisers will look at all of them, so leaving out the cheaper four makes $650k look safer than it is.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: Three sales might look like too small a sample, but Lena had seven; she kept only the ones that support a high price.

passage: People keep asking if keto beats low-fat for weight loss. I've linked three trials below where keto groups lost noticeably more weight at six months. Yes, the 12-month follow-ups mostly found no real difference, but almost nobody sticks to a diet for a full year anyway. The six-month data is what counts, and it's clear: keto wins.
cue: The six-month data is what counts, and it's clear: keto wins.
explanation: Rafael acknowledges the longer follow-ups but declares that only the six-month results count, because they favor keto. The fuller evidence, including a year out, doesn't show keto winning.

whyNot.fal_texas_sharpshooter: Rafael isn't spotting a pattern in random noise; he knows the full results and chooses the time frame that flatters keto.

title: Engagement survey: final numbers
passage: Hi all, final numbers are in. Following the rule we agreed on before launch, I removed 14 responses completed in under 30 seconds. With them excluded, 62% of staff rate their workload as manageable; with them included, it's 61%. Either way the conclusion holds: most staff say their workload is manageable, though a sizable minority don't.
cue: Following the rule we agreed on before launch
explanation: Dana did leave some data out, but by a rule set before anyone saw the results, and she shows the answer barely changes with it included. That's transparent, not selective.

whyNot.fal_cherry_picking: The exclusion rule was fixed in advance and the full-data result is reported too, so nothing inconvenient is being hidden.

passage: Lots of you asked whether the Mindloom app improves concentration. I found 20 studies. Fourteen had no control group, so I set those aside, following my usual rule. The six randomized trials found small or no effects, averaging out to almost nothing. So my honest answer: the app probably doesn't do much for focus, whatever its ads claim.
cue: Fourteen had no control group, so I set those aside, following my usual rule
explanation: Sam does narrow the evidence, but by a quality rule he applies consistently, and the result cuts against the product rather than toward an answer he wanted. Filtering by study quality is fair.

whyNot.fal_cherry_picking: Sam filters by a stated quality standard, not by which results he likes, and reports what the stronger studies actually found.
